title: check:budgets counts only the /_next/static chunks in the HTML, so Turnstile's api.js (27 KiB compressed) that /contact, /orders and the checkout form load at hydration is never measured; checkout's real initial JS is about 176 KiB, not 148.9
evidence: check-budgets.mjs:68 `if (!src.startsWith('/_next/static/')) continue` and it only reads `<script src>` tags (line 54). src/lib/turnstile.ts:32 injects `https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js?render=explicit&onload=…` from the ref callback of the form's box, i.e. on mount: ContactForm.tsx:217 (always), OrderPage.tsx:375 (RecoveryForm, shown when the tab holds no order link), CheckoutForm.tsx:750 (the form, shown as soon as the quote answers). Measured on the export with Playwright at 1440 (m-desk.json): /orders requests api.js at 213 ms and /contact at load, with no input. `curl -L` of that URL (2026-10-07): a 302 to /turnstile/v0/g/4df4a60fa397/api.js, then 86,732 bytes raw, 27,985 bytes served brotli, 27,685 gzip. The checkout HTML's own chunks are 148.9 KiB gzip (static.mjs, same as I50 (2)); contact 141.0, orders 147.8. The widget's iframe then loads its own challenge scripts, not measured here (blocked).
impact: The plan's gate 'public initial hydrated JS <150KiB gzip' (VERIFICATION.md:55, 'No silent relaxation') reports 1.1 KiB of headroom on checkout while a real buyer's phone downloads and runs about 176 KiB before paying (contact about 168, orders about 175). I50 (2) and docs/operations.md record the wrong number, and the next change is judged against it.
proposed_fix: In check-budgets, add Turnstile's measured size (a constant with the date it was measured, or a fetched size in a hosted check) to every page whose chunks contain `challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile`, and report it as its own line; then escalate the overrun with evidence as VERIFICATION.md requires (Cloudflare recommends loading the script early, so deferring it to the first focus on the form is a tradeoff to decide, not a free fix: AvailabilityForm.tsx:176 already arms it on interaction).
prior_overlap: I50 (2) and I49 (5) record the headroom from the HTML chunks only; TEST-E2E-16 (this audit) covers the missing product and post pages, not third-party scripts

title: public/_headers gives a cache lifetime only to /_next/static/*, so the fonts, every image, the video posters and the book PDF go out with Pages' default `max-age=0, must-revalidate` and are revalidated on every page load
evidence: public/_headers sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for `/_next/static/*` only (lines 47-49); no rule covers /fonts/*, /images/*, /brand/*, /book/* or /media/*. Cloudflare Pages (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/serving-pages/, updated 2026-04-21): '"Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate" is sent for cacheable assets', with ETags for revalidation. Measured initial requests per page at 1440 (m-desk.json): 3 to 5 Thmanyah fonts (78-83 KB each) and 2 to 26 images, e.g. /started: 4 fonts and 10 images (7 of them video posters).
impact: A returning visitor (every visit from a WhatsApp or Instagram link is a fresh page load) sends a conditional request for each font and image before it can use its cached copy: one extra round trip on the critical path for the fonts (a second flash of the fallback face on slow mobile links) and 20-plus revalidations per room page.
proposed_fix: Add rules for `/fonts/*` and `/images/*` (and `/brand/*`): the file names are not content-hashed, so a long max-age with revalidation, e.g. `Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, stale-while-revalidate=2592000`, or content-hashed names from prepare-media with `immutable`. Leave /book/* and /media/* as they are until I33 settles where the films live.
proof_recipe: On the hosted Pages preview: `curl -sI https://<preview>/fonts/thmanyah/thmanyahsans-Regular.woff2` shows `cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` today; after the fix it shows the new rule. In Chrome DevTools, reload /started twice: today every font and image row is a 304 revalidation; after the fix they come from the disk cache with no request.
prior_overlap: none (I32 (4) checks that _headers is served, not what it lacks)

evidence: ShelfRoomView.tsx:77 `{thuraDoor && }` takes Picture's default `loading = 'lazy'` (Picture.tsx:19) and no fetchPriority. out/shelf.html: ` 2444/2724/2696 ms, median 5584 -> 2696.

title: Every film's poster downloads with the page wherever the film sits: 278 KB on /started, 251 KB on /built and 138 KB on /passed compete with the fonts and the hero on a phone
evidence: VideoTile.tsx:87 `poster={`/${entry.poster}`}` on every `<video preload="none">`; a poster attribute has no lazy loading, so the browser fetches it when the element is parsed. Measured at 1440 (m-desk.json): /started requests all 7 posters at 58 ms, in parallel with the CSS and fonts, while the films sit at y=4214-4410. At 360 (4x CPU, slow 4G, m-mob.json) the 7 posters take 278 KB of the page's 886 KB initial load, the last one finishing at 6098 ms. A/B on the export with the posters of all but the first two films removed (exp2.mjs, 3 runs): /started 885 -> 651 KB with LCP unchanged (2720 -> 2704 ms, a text LCP); /built 780 -> 668 KB and LCP 3304 -> 3060 ms (its LCP is a poster in the first screen, which then gets the bandwidth). The comment at VideoTile.tsx:12 ('never loads a byte before the tap') holds for the film only.
impact: Phone visitors to the three film rooms spend 140-280 KB of their data and early bandwidth on pictures they may never scroll to; on /built the first-screen poster finishes about 0.25 s later than it could.
proposed_fix: Draw the poster as an `` (or the existing Picture) layered under the video and drop the `poster` attribute; keep `loading="eager"` for a tile in the first screen (the first two on /built). It works without JavaScript, unlike setting `poster` from an IntersectionObserver.
prior_overlap: none (VENDOR-PLAT-04 in this audit is about Range requests for the films themselves)

title: The cart, checkout and order pages are static shells only 50vh tall, so the footer sits in the first screen and the client island pushes it away: CLS 0.346 (cart), 0.415 (checkout), 0.119 (orders) at 360
evidence: store.module.css:28-30 `.page { min-block-size: 50vh; }` is the only height the money pages' `<main>` has (cart/page.tsx:14, checkout/page.tsx:23, orders/page.tsx:14, also checkout/return and notify); their content is a client island whose static state is one line («جارٍ تحميل السلة…», «جارٍ تحميل الطلب…») or a hidden status, so at 360x800 the footer starts at y=496 and at 1440x900 at y=561. Measured with a filled cart and every API call answered inside the browser by Playwright (cls-journey.mjs, quote mocked after 600 ms, nothing reached a server): 360 (4x CPU, slow 4G): /cart 0.346 (footer pushed out at 4.3 s, then 0.186 at 5.6 s), /checkout 0.415 (one shift at 5.5 s when the form replaces the loading line), /orders 0.119; 1440: 0.109, 0.273, 0.122. Same pages with only that rule changed to `min-block-size:100dvh` in the served CSS (cls-fix.mjs): 360: 0.085, 0.000, 0.006; 1440: 0.007, 0.000, 0.000. The cart's remaining 0.085 is PERF-08.
impact: The pages of the purchase journey fail the plan's CLS<0.1 goal by three to four times on a phone: the footer and its links slide away as the cart, the checkout form or the order appears, the page a buyer opens from the receipt mail included; a tap aimed at the footer or a field lands elsewhere.
proposed_fix: Give the island pages a shell that already reaches below the first screen: `min-block-size: 100dvh` (or `calc(100dvh - var(--header-h))`), measured above. `.page` is shared with the policies, the store grid and the product page, so either add a modifier class on the six island pages (cart, checkout, checkout/return, orders, notify/confirm, notify/unsubscribe) or accept the taller shell everywhere (only short pages change: their footer starts below the first screen). Then fix the cart's own re-layout (PERF-08).
prior_overlap: none (AUDIT-1, AUDIT-2 and the P08 round audits never measured layout shift on these pages)

title: The public layout preloads two 80 KB font files on every page at high priority; on a phone they take the bandwidth the hero needs, and removing them cuts LCP by 1.0-1.4 s on /, /journal and /book (0.4 s on /started)
evidence: layout.tsx:34-41 preloads thmanyahserifdisplay-Medium.woff2 (82,552 B) and thmanyahsans-Bold.woff2 (79,160 B) in every public page's head; the export carries each tag twice (React hoists a copy), and Chrome dedupes them (one request each). At 360x800, DPR 3, 4x CPU, DevTools slow 4G (562.5 ms RTT, 1.44 Mbit/s), the two start with the CSS at about 700 ms at High priority and end at 2.6-3.4 s (m-mob.json), sharing the link with the LCP image. A/B on the same export (local HTTP/1.1 server) with only the preload tags removed from the HTML (exp2.mjs, 3 runs each, medians): / LCP 3440 -> 2444 ms, /journal 3624 -> 2448, /book 4188 -> 2816, /started (text LCP) 2736 -> 2312, /policies/store (text LCP) 1916 -> 1904, /contact (text LCP) 2136 -> 2148; CLS / 0.003 -> 0.003, /journal 0.001 -> 0.001, /book 0.002 -> 0.002, /started 0.030 -> 0.033-0.036 (the later swap), /policies/store 0 -> 0, /contact 0.060 -> 0.060 (its own title swap, PERF-07). Marking them fetchpriority=low gains nothing (/ 3384, /journal 3728, /book 4372): the bytes still go first.
impact: On a mid-range phone on a slow mobile link, the pages led by a photo (home, المجلس, the book) paint their main image about a second later than they could; home and the journal miss the plan's LCP<2.5s goal because of it and would meet it without the preloads.
proposed_fix: Delete the two `<link rel="preload" as="font">` from the public layout; the faces are still found through the @font-face rules and swap in (font-display: swap). If the owner wants the title face early on the rooms, preload it only on pages whose LCP is that title, and re-measure.
proof_recipe: The A/B ran on a local HTTP/1.1 server; Pages serves HTTP/2 and 3 with its own prioritisation, so confirm the size of the gain there: deploy two Pages previews (today and without the two preload tags) and run Lighthouse mobile (or WebPageTest, Moto G4, 4G) 5 times each on /, /journal, /book and /started. Expected today: LCP on / and /journal above 2.5 s with the fonts finishing before the hero; without the preloads a lower median LCP and CLS still under 0.1.

title: On a slow phone the room heroes reflow when Thmanyah swaps in for the fallback face: /passed reaches CLS 0.111 at 360 (over the 0.1 goal), /contact 0.060, /started 0.033
evidence: globals.css:5-34 declares the faces with `font-display: swap` and nothing else; tokens.css:38 falls back to the generic `serif` (and `system-ui, sans-serif` for the body), with no metric-matched fallback (no size-adjust/ascent-override). At 360x800, 4x CPU, slow 4G the fonts land after first paint (2.6-4.8 s), so the poster-size title (`t-title`, clamp(68px, 12.4vw, 200px), RoomHero.tsx:34) and the lead (`t-lead`, RoomHero.tsx:38) re-wrap. shift.mjs, no input sent, mouse context, 3 runs: /passed 0.111/0.112/0.112, every run = a shift at about 3.05 s (0.083-0.085: the band under the hero moves 85 px as the title face swaps) plus one at 3.7-4.7 s (0.027: 45 px as the lead face swaps). /contact 0.060 (its title band moves 60 px) and /started 0.033 (45 px) in all runs. At 1440 unthrottled the same pages measure 0 (m-desk.json). With touch emulation Chrome flagged the first /passed shift `hadRecentInput` in 2 of 3 runs although no input was sent, which hides it from lab CLS; a real visitor gets no such pass.
impact: A phone visitor to مررتُ من هنا on a slow link sees the opening band jump twice, 85 px then 45 px, as they start reading; the room fails the plan's CLS<0.1 goal (VERIFICATION.md:55) in the lab. The size of the jump depends on the device's fallback face (the lab used Chromium on Windows; Android and iOS fall back to other Arabic faces), so the field number may be higher or lower.
proposed_fix: Give the stacks a metric-matched fallback: an `@font-face { font-family: 'Thmanyah Serif Display Fallback'; src: local('Noto Naskh Arabic'), local('Geeza Pro'), local('Times New Roman'); size-adjust/ascent-override/descent-override }` (and one for the sans) placed second in --font-display/--font-body, tuned so the hero keeps its line count; or reserve the hero title's and lead's block size. Re-measure at 360 on a slow profile and on a real Android and iPhone.
proof_recipe: Field or device proof: on the hosted preview, open /passed on a real Android phone and an iPhone with the network throttled to slow 4G (Chrome remote DevTools / Safari Web Inspector) and record the layout-shift entries (PerformanceObserver 'layout-shift', buffered) without touching the screen. Expected today: shifts of the band under the hero when the fonts arrive, summing near or above 0.1. After the fix: below 0.1 on both.
